title: "Meet the THIP data"
description: >
  What the inpatient data cover, their yearly scale, what a row represents,
  and how to interpret the main fields.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(width = 57)
```

This guide explains the data before you analyse them. The yearly row counts
below are **real THIP totals checked on 27 October 2026**. The small record
example is **entirely synthetic**. Query mechanics belong in
[Working with a database from R](database-from-r.html).

## 1. What the data cover

The inpatient tables contain hospital admission/claim records paid through the
National Health Security Office (NHSO). They describe the records available in
this source, rather than every hospital admission in Thailand. Other source
families, such as vaccinations, represent different events and need their own
interpretation.

Table names use Thai fiscal years in the Buddhist era. Fiscal year 2567 means
October 2023 to September 2024. The name is a convention, not a guarantee that
every admission date falls within those boundaries: check actual date coverage
when defining a study period.

```{r data-map, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat("```{=html}", "<div style=\"margin: 0.5rem 0 1.5rem;\">",
    readLines("figures/thip-data-map.svg"), "</div>", "```", sep = "\n")
```

## 2. Which tables are available, and their scale

The snapshot counts all stored rows in each named distributed table, using
`count()`. It includes repeated records if present; it is not a count of unique
admissions or people. The tables can change after the date checked.

```{r yearly-scale, echo = FALSE}
yearly_counts <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "thip_yearly_row_counts.csv", package = "thipR"),
  colClasses = "character"
)
scale <- data.frame(
  Table = yearly_counts$table_name,
  `Fiscal year (BE)` = yearly_counts$fiscal_year_be,
  `Stored rows` = format(as.numeric(yearly_counts$stored_rows),
                       big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(scale, caption = "Real THIP row-count snapshot — checked 27 October 2026.")
```

Inside THIP, list the tables currently available to your account with:

```{r discover-live, eval = FALSE}
con <- thip_connect()
thip_list_tables(con)
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```

`thip_list_tables()` hides names ending in `_local`, which refer to underlying
storage tables; use the distributed names shown above. The old function name
`thip_tables()` remains an alias. This page reads a saved snapshot when built;
it does not connect to THIP or refresh the counts automatically.

## 3. Follow a person across admissions {#one-record-versus-one-person}

The same person can have several inpatient records, including records in
different yearly tables. **Use `pid` to follow the person; use `tran_id` to
identify each record.** Both identifiers are text labels.

Let's ask for the records of two people in the **synthetic dataset supplied
with `thip_connect_example()`**. These identifiers are invented. We search two
yearly tables, then retrieve the matching records into R:

```{r example-query, message = FALSE}
library(thipR)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)

con_example <- thip_connect_example()
example_pids <- c(
  paste0("e127e59395cff1dffb934a865a29cc06",
         "d57d222ac30f3de095ea1d51"),
  paste0("004bdf60ba4d102bb7ff365ec4ac3b39",
         "a151bbd53689154c404a541a")
)

example_records <- thip_table(
  con_example,
  tables = c("nhso2565", "nhso2566"),
  .id = "source_table"
) |>
  filter(pid %in% example_pids) |>
  select(source_table, pid, tran_id, dateadm, datedsc) |>
  collect()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con_example)
```

The query returns **three records**. For readability, the table abbreviates
`tran_id` and labels the two full `pid` values Person A and Person B; the
dates and table names are the returned values.

```{r example-result, echo = FALSE}
example_records <- example_records[order(example_records$pid,
                                          example_records$dateadm), ]
example_records$person <- c("A", "B")[match(example_records$pid, example_pids)]
example_records <- example_records[order(example_records$person,
                                          example_records$dateadm), ]
stopifnot(nrow(example_records) == 3L,
          length(unique(example_records$pid)) == 2L,
          length(unique(example_records$tran_id)) == 3L)
display_records <- data.frame(
  Person = paste("Person", example_records$person),
  `Record ID (shortened)` = paste0(substr(example_records$tran_id, 1, 8), "…"),
  `Source table` = example_records$source_table,
  Admitted = example_records$dateadm,
  Discharged = example_records$datedsc,
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(display_records, caption = "Records returned from the synthetic example.")
```

The timeline shows those same three records, with dates displayed in a more
readable format:

```{r admission-timeline, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
example_records$admitted <- as.Date(example_records$dateadm, "%Y%m%d")
example_records$discharged <- as.Date(example_records$datedsc, "%Y%m%d")
stopifnot(nrow(example_records) == 3L,
          length(unique(example_records$tran_id)) == 3L,
          !anyNA(example_records$admitted),
          !anyNA(example_records$discharged))
x_date <- function(date) {
  160 + as.numeric(as.Date(date) - as.Date("2022-09-15")) / 30 * 540
}
boundary <- x_date("2022-10-01")
svg <- c(
  '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 760 370" role="img" aria-labelledby="timeline-title timeline-desc">',
  '<title id="timeline-title">Three synthetic records, two people, across two fiscal years</title>',
  '<desc id="timeline-desc">Person A has a same-day admission on 19 September 2022 in nhso2565, then another stay on 8 to 9 October in nhso2566. Person B stays from 4 to 6 October in nhso2566. The fiscal year changes on 1 October.</desc>',
  '<style>.tl-text{font:18px system-ui,sans-serif;fill:#334155}.tl-small{font:16px system-ui,sans-serif;fill:#475569}.tl-bold{font:600 20px system-ui,sans-serif;fill:#0f172a}</style>',
  '<rect width="760" height="370" rx="8" fill="#fff"/>',
  '<text x="24" y="28" class="tl-bold">Three records, two people</text>',
  '<text x="24" y="49" class="tl-small">Synthetic example · September–October 2022</text>',
  sprintf('<rect x="160" y="65" width="%s" height="225" fill="#f1f5f9"/>', boundary - 160),
  sprintf('<rect x="%s" y="65" width="%s" height="225" fill="#eff6ff"/>', boundary, 700 - boundary),
  '<text x="180" y="89" class="tl-bold">nhso2565</text>',
  sprintf('<text x="%s" y="89" class="tl-bold">nhso2566</text>', boundary + 18),
  sprintf('<line x1="%s" x2="%s" y1="100" y2="290" stroke="#94a3b8" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/>', boundary, boundary),
  '<text x="24" y="155" class="tl-bold">Person A</text>',
  '<text x="24" y="245" class="tl-bold">Person B</text>',
  '<path d="M160 150H700 M160 240H700" stroke="#cbd5e1"/>')
for (i in seq_len(nrow(example_records))) {
  record <- example_records[i, ]
  x1 <- x_date(record$admitted)
  x2 <- x_date(record$discharged)
  y <- if (record$person == "A") 150 else 240
  color <- if (record$person == "A") "#2563eb" else "#0f766e"
  label <- if (record$admitted == record$discharged) {
    paste(format(record$admitted, "%d %b"), "(same day)")
  } else {
    paste0(format(record$admitted, "%d"), "–",
           format(record$discharged, "%d %b"))
  }
  svg <- c(svg,
    sprintf('<line x1="%s" x2="%s" y1="%s" y2="%s" stroke="%s" stroke-width="10" stroke-linecap="round"/>', x1, x2, y, y, color),
    sprintf('<circle cx="%s" cy="%s" r="5" fill="%s"/>', x1, y, color),
    sprintf('<text x="%s" y="%s" text-anchor="middle" class="tl-text">%s</text>', (x1 + x2) / 2, y - 18, label))
}
for (date in c("2022-09-15", "2022-10-01", "2022-10-15")) {
  x <- x_date(date)
  svg <- c(svg, sprintf('<text x="%s" y="313" text-anchor="middle" class="tl-small">%s</text>', x, format(as.Date(date), "%d %b")))
}
svg <- c(svg,
  '<text x="24" y="350" class="tl-small">Marks show individual records, from admission to discharge.</text>',
  '</svg>')
cat("```{=html}", paste(svg, collapse = "\n"), "```", sep = "\n")
```

Person A's second admission is in a new table, but it is still the same person.
This matters for two common questions:

- **How many people were admitted?** These records contain one person in 2565
  and two in 2566. Across both years there are **two distinct people**, not three.
- **What happened after an admission?** Following A into the next table finds
  another admission. Looking only in the first yearly table would miss it.

A repeat admission is not automatically a duplicate record. With real data,
check identifier uniqueness and linkage before counting people or constructing
follow-up; define which records represent separate encounters for your study.

## 4. The main columns

| Group | Fields | What to look for |
|---|---|---|
| Identifiers | `pid`, `tran_id` | Person and record identifiers; keep as text |
| Demographics | `age_y`, `sex` | Recorded age and sex codes |
| Admission and discharge | `dateadm`, `datedsc`, `dischs`, `discht` | Dates, condition at discharge, and discharge type |
| Diagnoses and procedures | `pdx`, `sdx1`–`sdx20`, `proc1`–`proc21` | Principal diagnosis, secondary diagnoses, procedures |
| Death | `death_date` | Linked person-level death date |
| Geography | `health_region`, `superdistrict` | Health-region code and grouped facility geography |

### Diagnoses and procedures

`pdx` is the principal diagnosis; `sdx1`–`sdx20` hold secondary diagnoses.
The dictionary labels diagnoses as ICD-10; Thai coding uses ICD-10-TM.
Procedures use ICD-9-CM. Check how punctuation and codes are stored before
applying a code list; [Flag conditions](condition-flags.html) covers matching.

`dischs` describes the condition at discharge, while `discht` describes how the
patient left. `death_date` is a linked death date, not by itself evidence of
death during a particular admission: compare it with the stay's dates.

The dictionary defines `superdistrict` as the treating facility's grouped
location, not the patient's residence. `health_region` has codes 01–13;
confirm its geographic basis before using it as a residence measure.

Use `thip_fields` for documented definitions and code meanings, and
`thip_columns()` for the current table schema:

```{r field-reference, eval = FALSE}
thip_fields
# With an open THIP connection:
thip_columns(con, "nhso2568")
```

The dictionary and live schema serve different purposes; a new field may appear
before it has a documented interpretation.

## 5. Storage conventions before analysis

The yearly inpatient columns were stored as text (`String`) when the snapshot
was checked, including ages, dates and identifiers.

| Kind | Illustrative value | How to treat it |
|---|---|---|
| Number stored as text | `"102"` | Convert before numeric comparison; text `"99"` sorts after `"102"` |
| Code | `"01"` | Keep as text to preserve leading zeros |
| Admission/discharge date | `"20231015"` | Parse explicitly as `%Y%m%d` |
| Death date | `"2023-10-15"` | Parse explicitly as `%Y-%m-%d` |
| Empty text | `""` | Check separately from SQL NULL / R `NA` |

Check actual values and missingness before conversion. [From question to
cohort](question-to-cohort.html) shows explicit date conversion;
[Check before you trust](data-checks.html) covers invalid values and duplicates.
